analysis:
This PR contains only docs and changelog files, with no executable source. The security-relevant claims are:
(1) docs/architecture/security/attestation.md moves centralized authorization to the external Layr-Labs/darkbloom-platform. It says missing recurring receipt/risk evidence no longer blocks basic serving (head line 112). This conflicts with the threat model's 'every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt' (TB-011, T-053..T-057); reported as a finding.
(2) The docs describe a provider same-process endpoint-resumption responder. The reference is to the protocol-1 'endpoint-custody' response, in CoordinatorClient.connectAndRun and ProviderLoop+Serve.swift. Claims: a fresh nonce per socket, reuse of the in-memory X25519 key (A-003), no Apple operation, no local trust. Not verifiable here. The next pass should check nonce/origin binding, replay of the custody proof across sockets, and whether it can substitute for the endpoint binding in TB-011.
(3) The changelog claims logout-token issuer binding and revocation, a resume control-frame size limit enforced before decode, UTF-16/32 JSON rejection, and revocation-request authority preservation. The implementing code is not in this batch. The next pass should check SSRF or credential leakage to a wrong issuer (A-008) and parser-bypass handling.
(4) The native-qualification diagnostic is described as opt-in and isolated. The next pass should confirm it cannot grant serving or replace the installed provider.
Coverage limit: no implementation was reviewed; the resumption and logout claims are unverified.

findings.detail: The new paragraph states that missing recurring receipt/risk evidence neither blocks otherwise qualified basic serving nor triggers further assertions. It also says only an established exact identity may retain last-known policy within proof and administrative ceilings. It cites an external darkbloom-platform revision for these semantics. The canonical threat model and the removed text require every serving grant to have a fresh verified risk receipt and complete metric. They also say failed reads never extend ceilings and that receipt renewal is independent. TB-011 and T-053/T-054/T-055/T-057 therefore no longer describe the cited authorization semantics. A provider whose receipt or risk evidence is missing or stale could now serve under the platform policy. Receipt-based Sybil, risk and capacity checks would then gate only rewards and MDM-removal readiness, not serving. The retained coordinator in this repo may still enforce the old rule, so the docs and the threat model now disagree. Fix: update TB-011, T-053..T-057 and A-016 to state which authorization authority applies. Define the retained-policy ceilings and the effect of missing receipts on serving. Mark the old receipt-required statements as superseded or snapshot-only.
findings.title: Docs adopt platform policy that drops the receipt requirement for basic serving, contradicting the threat model
